featured_reviews.name: The Lucky Guide
featured_reviews.review_text:
One night, I had this terrible craving to eat khichidi, and I remembered that someone suggested trying this place out as they have great vegetarian options. I browsed their menu on Google and found a mixed vegetable khichidi to be interesting. I called and placed the order, and I was told in 30 minutes that the parcel would arrive and the bill was 170/-.

Though I found it to be expensive for a simple khichidi, I was expecting really mind-blowing with all the suggestions I received. I waited, and I waited, and I waited till I finally lost patience as the time frame crossed an hour and still no khichidi. I call, and this girl/woman/lady answers the call and gives me jazz about why the order is taking so long, cleverly done coz when a female answers the call out of traditional respect we don't scream and shout at them and with this these people get away with what they do.

All said and done, the khichidi arrived cold and tasted very basic. In the name of vegetables, it had beans, carrots, and capsicum. The portion was ok, not great, nor bad. It's definitely not worth paying 170/-, maybe what I can do is cook a khichidi one day and ask them to taste it for reference when they decide to charge you 170/- for food that tastes like it was cooked for a hospital and served cold.

This place is no longer on my try again list. Maybe the other items on the menu might be good, and people like what they serve; however, I've not seen a lot of people who actually know what food is all about.

featured_reviews.name: Ishayu Sonawane
featured_reviews.review_text: It was a really good experience. The owner Russell Pinto himself was attending us. The food was really good. We ordered a handful of dishes and drinks. We started with their iconic The Posh sando. It had really juicy Tenderloin stake with grilled onions and mushrooms. The bread was crazy good. Crusty on the outside, soft and fluffy on the inside. It is the highlight of the sandwich. We also tried the chimichurri steak sando which had their in house chimichurri spread which was really good and spicy. The goan pork rost sandwich was also a good one. The pork on the inside was a bit dry but it paired well with the liquidy side which tasted like soup. It was a really good pork sando. The korean fried chicken sando was okay-okayish. It was not that great but also not that bad. I think sandos taste good only when they have buff or pork inside them. The spicy BBQ chicken wings had a veryy tangy taste to them which made them hard to like. Honestly not my type of taste. The pesto spaghetti chicken was good but half people on our table didn't like it. The pesto sauce was really good and the spaghetti was also fine. It had nice grilled chicken which was pretty tasty. We also ordered their kombucha which is a non alcoholic fermented drink which was reallyyy good. Also their iced tea was delightful. At the end the chef Russell Pinto gave us two complementary on-house serradura which were so damm tasty dessert. They were really creamy and had layers of biscuit crumbs on the inside. A perfect way to end your lunch. Serradura is a must try. Thank you chef Russell for the on-house desserts! The service was top notch. Chef Russell was himself serving us and was looking after our table. We really appreciate him. The bill came out to be almost three thousand rupees with taxes which is pretty reasonable for 6 people. Overall a superb experience. Will definitely go back for another sando. Overall a 9 on 10.

featured_reviews.name: simonti bisi
featured_reviews.review_text: I had heard a lot of rave reviews of this place to decided to try it during my stay at my parent’s place in Malad. We ordered for the chicken cafreal sando, korean fried chicken, roast pork and chorizo sandos. The chicken cafreal was hands down delicious. The chicken was moist and cafreal masala was also delicious. They use a special goan bread called Katre Pav which has a crunchy exterior and is soft inside. I would give this sandwich a 10/10. My hopes were very high after the chicken cafreal and then unfortunately, it came crashing down. The pork sandwich was a big let-down. The pork was dry and it was hard to swallow. A little bit of freshness in between the breads would have been nice but I doubt it would be sufficient to save the sandwich. The Chorizo sando was just chorizo and poiee. That’s it. Something which even I make at home. The Korean chicken was better than the other sando’s at the most decent. So if you decide to order from here just go for the chicken cafreal.

featured_reviews.name: Vidhisha Umrakia
featured_reviews.review_text:
Let me first start with a Thank you to the courteous member of the staff DHARMENDRA because with out his support I would have not be able to have such an amazing experience.
I had hosted a birthday party and from a month back I was visiting this place to just be sure I am choosing a right place for a family gathering and to my surprise I wasn’t wrong for a single moment.

Starting with the ambience - Simple yet classy.
Food - each and every item was delicious starters to mock tails
Main course to dessert each and every time was must have.
Starters were
1. Garden tiki - don’t be in the interpretation that it would be like hara bhara kebab it was the yummiest veg starter I had.
2. Thread Paneer - again a different concept of paneer where every guest kept on asking for it.
3. Fries - served freshly hot and crispy

Main Course -
1. Pink Sauce pasta - AMAZING … the flavours is still lingering in my mouth freshest cooked and served for a single moment I did not feel bland or over cooked.
2. Garden pizza - served on flat bread cheesiest and yummiest.
3. Veg Vilayati - not spicy but still not disappointing.
4. DD special Chinese bowl - to say it was like a regular fried rice and gravy Wo exotic veggies and paneer but again the flavour each content had was too delicious.
Dessert - Palak Halwa there renowned dish was again good but since it shouldn’t become too sweet so we had asked them to serve it with vanilla ice team and the great pet was they did serve exceptionally for us.
Mocktail - all exceptionally good.
DD shooters
Virgin Mojito
Fruit punch

Great great experience I had ever had. It would must to visit next time for us. I am sure you’ll will have a great experience.

If you’ll plan to arrange and a party this can be in your list and especially if you get the chance to be guided by Dharmendra it will be a great experience.

All in all so visit. 10 on 10

The hot garlic  Eggs are really tasty, it was made purely from garlic & green onions. The taste was super yumm. The gravy was too good, egg sholay was really delicious & worth trying. The dish was loaded with stuffed boiled eggs & wrapped in omlette which was again topped in creamy tomato gravy.

featured_reviews.name: Parth Mangukiya
featured_reviews.review_text: I must say that this restaurant serves incredible egg-related dishes; I ordered egg masala bhel and surti patra, and the food was far superior to global fusion. The restaurant is small and homey, but the food is excellent! I read a lot of negative reviews about the atmosphere and service. I didn't have to deal with anything like that. I'd go a hundred times just to enjoy the food instead of eating bland at a fancy restaurant. My recommendation is to order/visit this restaurant solely for the pleasure of your taste buds. I also appreciated the proprietor's hospitality! I wish I could order or eat more, but the food was extremely filling! Next time, I'll bring my friends or family to experience more variety!

featured_reviews.name: Hamza Kagzi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Egg Station is a very nice outlet. On new link road, Malad west.
Excellent, unassuming and wonderful find. A wide variety and fine value tasting menu. Exciting food with high quality presentation, service and inventiveness. A highlight of Malad. Will not be disappointing, it's really worth it.

It is not a huge outlet, but it has amazing decor and lighting, which makes it truly amazing. Services were very quick and staff was very knowledgeable about the menu.

Each and every dish we had was amazing in taste and well presented. Most of the dishes are made with cheese and loaded with butter which makes them very tasty and heavy.

What we ordered

Kashmiri Bhurji : The Kashmiri Bhurji was well cooked with mixed spices and served hot with bread. The dish was extremely tasty and the bread was loaded with butter.

Mexican Egg Roll: This was a thick gravy topped with egg rolls served hot with breads. Yet another dish that was so amazing and tasty. Must try.

Egg chips: This was a unique dish made with eggs. It looks like kabab and is served with mint chutney.

A must try resturant for egg eaters!!!

Food 5/5
Services 5/5
Ambience 5/5

featured_reviews.name: Traveller Munda
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Egg Station in Thane today for lunch with a friend of mine as I was craving for Egg varieties. It is a small but cutely designed joint. They have a good spread of Egg varieties in Mumbai style and most importantly in Surti style.
For starter I tried Egg Masala Bhel which set my mood just perfect
Red Paplet & Ghotala Rice were the mains I ordered.
This dishes clearly satisfied my cravings & reminded me of eggs tried in Surat. Loved trying this place & it's fixed in my list forever for having Eggs.

featured_reviews.name: Manav Rajani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Egg station - this is a one stop for all the egg cravings.

Compact and nice this place is a egg paradise for all the eggetarians and the ones crazy behind having to taste different egg plates.

They have around 57 kinds of egg dishes and you’d be amazed to see how well almost each dish is sorted and made.

Being the only one i tried the Surti ghotala - mixture of boiled eggs and raw eggs with their famous green gravy. Has the right garlic punch. Served with butter pav and a mini salad which is chopped onion / tomatoes and Kashmiri mirchi sprinkled on top.

Great concept and place overall - will come back for more.
